page: Google Cloud Platform a2-ultragpu-4g is an accelerator-optimized server configured with four NVIDIA Ampere A100 GPUs, providing a total of 320 GB of VRAM. The host system features an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs operating at a base frequency of 2.2 GHz. System memory totals 680.0 GB, yielding approximately 14.17 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided by 1608 GB of NVMe SSD capacity.

Benchmark data indicates that single-core CPU performance is in the bottom 25%, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core tests. However, multi-core CPU capabilities and memory bandwidth fall into the middle 50% tier. The server excels in large-scale model execution, achieving top-tier performance in LLM inference prompt processing across 135M, 7B, and 70B models, as well as top-tier text generation speeds for 7B and 70B models.

This server represents a high-density resource profile where the cost efficiency is centered on GPU-intensive workloads rather than general-purpose compute. The tradeoff involves lower single-threaded CPU performance and average multi-core CPU execution relative to the substantial GPU and memory allocation. It is designed for workloads that offload processing to the GPU accelerators rather than relying on raw CPU clock speeds.

The hardware configuration is designed for large language model inference, deep learning training, and data science pipelines. The combination of 320 GB of GPU VRAM, 680 GB of system memory, and local NVMe SSD storage supports large-scale parallel processing tasks, while the system is less optimal for single-threaded applications or basic web serving.
